newsitem.title: USA: U.S. fund managers remain long on US debt - survey.
newsitem.headline: U.S. fund managers remain long on US debt - survey.

text.p: Money managers extended duration exposure and lowered their cash holdings on their U.S. debt portfolios over the past week, suggesting that bond investors are still bullish, according to a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates.
"Indications are that there will be more extension going into the quarter-end, as the expected participation rate is high, with players long and bullish," it said.
In the week ended June 17, the cash/assets ratio fell to 8.87 percent from 8.90 percent on an arithmetic basis and rose to 6.62 percent from 6.52 percent on a weighted basis.
The survey's actual/target duration index rose to 99.52 percent from 98.72 percent on an arithmetic basis and rose to 99.60 percent from 99.49 percent on a weighted basis.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
The survey's bear/bull index rose to 4.87 from 4.65 on an arithmetic basis. It inched up to 4.55 from 4.50 on an asset-weighted basis.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
Twenty-two percent of the portfolio managers surveyed said they were planning to be active in the coming week, up from 9.0 percent the week ending June 10.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
